short_description.id: Gangcheori adalah monster berbentuk naga dalam mitologi Korea.
short_description.en: Gangcheori is a dragon-shaped monster of Korean mythology.

long_description.id: Gangcheori (강철이; 強鐵) adalah monster berbentuk naga dalam mitologi Korea yang dikenal sejak abad ke-17 dan sejak dulu populer di seluruh negeri. Nama lainnya meliputi Gangcheol, Kkangcheol, dan Ggoangcheol.
long_description.en: Gangcheori (강철이; 強鐵), a monster shaped like a dragon, belongs to Korean mythology, entered tradition in the 17th century, and has long been popular across the country. Other names include Gangcheol, Kkangcheol, and Ggoangcheol.

long_description.id: Salah satu catatan paling awal adalah Jibong Yuseol (1614): seorang lelaki tua di pedesaan memberi tahu pengarang Lee Soo-kwang tentang monster yang membakar habis segalanya sejauh beberapa mil. Yeolha Ilgi mencatat peribahasa bahwa di mana gangcheol pergi, musim gugur pun seperti musim semi, yang berarti kekeringan dan gagal panen.
long_description.en: One of the earliest records is the Jibong Yuseol (1614): an old man in the countryside told the author Lee Soo-kwang about a monster that burns down everything for a few miles. The Yeolha Ilgi records a saying that where gangcheol goes, autumn is like spring, meaning drought and a poor harvest.

long_description.id: Para penulis berbeda pendapat: Seongho Saseol menyebutnya merusak pertanian lewat hujan lebat, sedangkan Anyeop Gi menggambarkan makhluk mirip anak kuda di rawa Gimpo yang menyebabkan kekeringan. Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Korea, bencana perusak pertanian secara umum tampaknya dialihkan sebagai perbuatan gangcheori.
long_description.en: The writers disagreed: the Seongho Saseol says it ruins farming through heavy rain, whereas the Anyeop Gi describes a foal-like creature in a Gimpo swamp that causes drought. According to Korean Wikipedia, natural disasters ruining farming in general seem to have been attributed to gangcheori.

statement.id: Dalam Yeolha Ilgi, penutur menyebut makhluk itu bernama gangcheol (罡鐵) dan mengutip peribahasa rakyat Korea 'di mana gangcheol pergi, musim gugur pun menjadi musim semi', artinya ia mendatangkan kekeringan dan gagal panen; orang miskin yang rencananya gagal menyebutnya 'musim gugur gangcheol'.
statement.en: In the Yeolha Ilgi, the speaker says the creature is named gangcheol (罡鐵) and cites the Korean folk saying 'where gangcheol goes, autumn becomes spring', meaning it brings drought and a poor harvest; poor people whose plans go awry speak of 'gangcheol's autumn'.

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Korea menyebut bahwa Yi Su-gwang, penulis Jibong Yuseol, menganggap makhluk pembakar tumbuhan sejauh beberapa ri itu sebagai monster bi (蜚) dalam Shanhaijing.
statement.en: Korean Wikipedia says Yi Su-gwang, author of the Jibong Yuseol, took the monster that burns all plants for several ri around to be the monster bi (蜚) of the Shanhaijing.

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Korea, Seongho Saseol karya Yi Ik (1740) menyebut gangcheori sebagai makhluk yang merusak pertanian bukan lewat kekeringan melainkan hujan lebat, dan Yi Ik menganggapnya sama dengan naga beracun (dokryong) dari Tiongkok.
statement.en: According to Korean Wikipedia, Yi Ik's Seongho Saseol (1740) describes gangcheori as a creature that ruins farming not by drought but by heavy rain, and Yi Ik took it to be the same as the Chinese poison dragon (dokryong).

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Korea, Anyeop Gi karya Yi Deok-mu menggambarkannya sebagai makhluk mirip anak kuda yang hidup di rawa Gimpo dan menyebabkan kekeringan, dan Yi Deok-mu menganggapnya sama dengan makhluk hou (犼) Tiongkok.
statement.en: According to Korean Wikipedia, Yi Deok-mu's Anyeop Gi describes it as a creature like a foal living in a swamp in Gimpo and causing drought, and Yi Deok-mu took it to be the same as the Chinese creature hou (犼).

short_description.id: Garkain adalah sosok manusia-roh bersayap kulit dalam mitologi Australian Aboriginal di Arnhem Land yang membekap mangsanya [garkain-c01] [garkain-c02].
short_description.en: Garkain is a winged spirit-man in Arnhem Land Australian Aboriginal lore who smothers victims with folds of skin [garkain-c01] [garkain-c02].

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Australian Aboriginal di kawasan Arnhem Land, Northern Territory, Garkain digambarkan sebagai sosok manusia-roh yang mendiami hutan lebat Magurlipun di dekat muara Liverpool River [garkain-c01]. Tubuhnya seukuran manusia biasa dan memiliki kemampuan berjalan maupun terbang, tetapi tidak dapat berbicara serta tidak mengetahui cara membuat api [garkain-c04].
long_description.en: In the Australian Aboriginal traditions of Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, Garkain is known as a spirit-man haunting the dense jungle of Magurlipun near the Liverpool River's mouth [garkain-c01]. Sized like an ordinary man, he can both walk and take flight, yet lacks speech and fire-making skills [garkain-c04].

long_description.id: Jika ada pengelana yang memasuki wilayahnya, Garkain akan membunuh mereka dengan cara membekap menggunakan lipatan kulit longgar di lengan dan kakinya [garkain-c02]. Ia merupakan pemburu nokturnal yang tidur di siang hari di bawah tumpukan dedaunan hutan [garkain-c03].
long_description.en: Should an intruder venture into his territory, Garkain suffocates them beneath the loose folds of skin along his limbs [garkain-c02]. Operating as a nocturnal hunter, he spends the daylight hours resting under piles of jungle leaves [garkain-c03].

long_description.id: Pada 1957, antropolog Charles P. Mountford menyumbangkan lukisan kulit kayu eukaliptus bergambar Garkain (1948 atau 1949) dari komunitas Aborigin Gunbalanya di Arnhem Land barat kepada Art Gallery of South Australia di Adelaide. Lukisan itu memperlihatkan lipatan kulit makhluk tersebut, dan kakinya digambarkan sebagai jejak kaki, seperti lazim pada penggambaran makhluk roh dan manusia.
long_description.en: The anthropologist Charles P. Mountford presented the Art Gallery of South Australia in Adelaide, in 1957, with a bark painting of Garkain made on eucalyptus (1948 or 1949) in the Gunbalanya community of western Arnhem Land. It shows the creature's flaps of skin and draws his feet as footprints, as is usual in depictions of spirit and human beings.

long_description.id: Mountford mencatat kemiripan antara Garkain dan Warraguk, dan mengamati bahwa secara keseluruhan Garkain tidak seditakuti makhluk roh lain di daerah itu seperti Namarakain dan Nabudi.
long_description.en: Mountford noted similarities between Garkain and Warraguk, and observed that overall Garkain was not as feared as other local spirit beings such as the Namarakain and the Nabudi.

selection_criteria: computeFillStatus must be lengkap-informasi: complete, valid research without an approved image.
No active editorial artwork and no permanent artwork exclusion.
The accepted research entry is embedded unchanged; the image may only depict what its claims document.
Creatures an earlier batch left out keep that reason as catatan_sebelumnya; the generator may decline them with status tidak-digambar.

user_policy.name: sangar
user_policy.intent: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
user_policy.subject: The being dominates the frame and is clearly the subject. Head, eyes and distinguishing traits are readable even at thumbnail size. Never a landscape without the being, never a human who could be a passer-by, never a farm animal at pasture.
user_policy.moment: Depict a moment, not a pose: hunting, emerging, striking, commanding, towering, descending, tearing through weather or ground. Gaze and posture confront or loom over the viewer. Standing still and facing the camera with a neutral expression is not acceptable.
user_policy.effects: Visible power is wanted and may be strong, but every effect must come from a power, domain, attribute, habitat or deed documented in the research claims of that being, and it must act physically on the world: ground cracking, water rearing, trees bending, lightning striking, flame consuming, fog pouring, bodies of victims turned to stone. No generic glowing envelope, neon outline, energy ribbons, floating runes or luminous coloured mist. If the research documents no power, build menace from anatomy, scale, moment, light and setting instead, and record that in artistic_choices.
user_policy.fidelity: Anatomy, attributes, number of heads, eyes, limbs and iconography follow the research claims exactly. Effects and atmosphere add power; they never replace or invent anatomy. Fully opaque clothing where a humanlike form is clothed; no nudity, no explicit gore.
user_policy.composition: Low camera angle; monumental or predatory scale with small environmental references when size is documented, otherwise dominance through tight framing and foreshortening. Strong silhouette, high contrast, cinematic low-key lighting from one dominant source (moon, fire, lightning, dying sun), rim light, dust, smoke, rain or spray. Tactile surfaces: wet scales, matted fur, cracked skin, rust, weathered cloth, stone.
user_policy.setting: The place its stories name: graveyard, swamp, sea cliff, battlefield, celestial palace, desert storm. Weather and time of day heighten threat or majesty. Palette is dark and warm with one strong accent, consistent with the collection; no pastel, no flat even daylight.
user_policy.respect: Living religions (Hindu, Buddhist, Shinto, Abrahamic and folk deities still worshipped) are majestic and overwhelming rather than monstrous: cosmic scale, divine radiance from documented attributes, the elements they rule in motion. Malevolent beings are menacing. Literary beings follow their source text, never a film, game, anime or comic design.
user_policy.aniconic: If the research documents no bodily form at all, either depict the documented manifestation as an active, overwhelming force (the sky itself splitting, a storm swallowing the steppe) with the choice recorded in artistic_choices, or decline the entry with status tidak-digambar. A calm scene without agency fails.
user_policy.self_check: Before accepting an image the generator answers all of these with yes: the being dominates the frame; it still looks dangerous or majestic at 200 px; there is a moment, not a static pose; each visible effect points to a claim id; head, eye and limb counts match the claims; no text, watermark, border or borrowed design; it would not be rejected as ordinary person, ordinary animal, landscape only, or cute and calm. One no means regenerate, keep the rejected attempt as history, up to three attempts.
user_policy.style: Square premium painterly cinematic illustration in the house style of the existing artwork, more dramatic and higher contrast. No text, labels, logo, border or watermark.
user_policy.sources: Never copy designs from films, games, anime or comics (modern_depictions). Every design is original and sourced from the accepted research.
